source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Whether the dosage form can be safely manipulated; modified-release and enteric-coated products may not be crushable","B":"Whether the tablet is large enough to crush; formulation design does not affect tube-administration safety","C":"Whether tube feeding is running, because all solid oral medications are safe to crush when nutrition is infusing","D":"Whether the client can taste the medicine, because taste determines whether a tablet can be crushed safely"}}
source_row.rationale: Medication suitability must be checked before crushing for tube administration. Modified-release and enteric-coated products are common examples that may be inappropriate to crush because manipulation can alter release, efficacy, safety, or tube patency.
source_row.source_detail: JPEN 2023, PMID 36847617: evaluation of oral dosage forms for feeding-tube administration and appropriateness of crushing/manipulation; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: PubMed — Developing Guidance for Feeding Tube Administration of Oral Medications
source_row.stem: Before crushing a tablet for administration through an enteral feeding tube, what should the nurse verify?
